overview.text: The Southwestern Speckled Rattlesnake is a medium-sized venomous rattlesnake of rocky country in the south-western USA and north-western Mexico. Its colours match the local rocks.

identification.text: Pink, brown, grey, yellow or nearly white, speckled with black and white - matching the rocks and soil where it lives.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 3 ft (90 cm) on average, sometimes over 4 ft.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern California, southern Nevada, south-western Utah and western Arizona, and north-western Sonora and northern Baja California.

habitat.text: Rocky hillsides, canyons, slopes and ledges.

behaviour.text: Mostly active at night, sheltering in crevices and burrows by day; more active by day in cooler months.

diet.text: Mostly small mammals, plus birds and lizards.
